newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca seen next for share split.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca seen next for share split.

text.p: British pharmaceuticals and speciality chemicals company Zeneca Group Plc is increasingly expected to follow the lead of its UK rival SmithKline Beecham Plc and split its surging stock, analysts said on Wednesday.
On Tuesday, SmithKline announced a two-for-one split of its shares and American Depository Receipts (ADRs) as a direct response to "the significant rise" in its share price.
SmithKline has more than doubled in value over the past two years to trade at 1210 pence late Wednesday.
Zeneca too has soared in value since its was demerged from Imperial Chemical Industries Plc in June 1993 at 632 pence per share, and has also doubled in value over the past two years.

The company, which announces interim results on August 7, broke firmly through the 20 pound barrier late last month, touching an all-time peak of 23 pounds per share on July 16. It has since drifted back to trade around 2055 pence late on Wednesday.
It is one of only two companies in the FTSE index of 100 leading shares with a share price above 20 stg, and one of only 14 above 10 stg.
"It would make even more sense for them," said Kleinwort Benson analyst Stephen Putnam.
Putnam said, however, that the change was largely psychological.
"The British don't like great share prices. Between five and ten pounds people like," he added.
Another analyst said "It always seems a pointless exercise to me...for some reason small shareholders seem to like it. Why not make small shareholders happy?"
Analysts said although the change is largely technical, share splits are often followed by strong gains in the share price.
"The historic performance of the shares post similar splits has generally been excellent," analysts at Salomon Brothers said in a note on SmithKline Beecham on Wednesday.
Some newspaper reports even attributed SmithKline's strong gains on Wednesday to its share split rather than its first-half performance.
Others trying to attract more small investors through share splits this year have included the world's biggest company, Royal Dutch/Shell and business services operator Rentokil Initial Plc.
